earnings.title: INVESTOR RELATIONS CONTACT:
highlights: Net sales of $1.622 billion, increased 42.2% from the year-ago quarter and up 9.2% sequentially.

On a GAAP basis: gross profit of 65.9%; operating income of $464.5 million and 28.6% of net sales; net income attributable to common stockholders of $373.6 million; and EPS of $0.68 per diluted share.
On a Non-GAAP basis: gross profit of 66.5%; operating income of $639.9 million and 39.5% of net sales; net income of $559.2 million; and EPS of $0.97 per diluted share.

quotes.text: Our September quarter net sales were above the high end of our guidance, increasing 42.2% year over year and 9.2% sequentially to $1.622 billion.
quotes.by: Steve Sanghi, Microchip’s President and Chief Executive Officer

quotes.text: Our September quarter results reflect ongoing operational improvements, with non-GAAP operating expenses growing well below net sales and supporting higher profitability.
quotes.by: Corporate Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer

outlook: The midpoint of our guidance provided on August 6, 2026 was net sales of $1.604 billion.
Our guidance provided on August 6, 2026 was GAAP EPS per diluted share of $0.53 to $0.54.
Our guidance provided on August 6, 2026 was Non-GAAP EPS per diluted share of $0.91 to $0.95.
Capital expenditures for the quarter ending December 31, 2026 are expected to be about $35 million.

items.heading: Our operating results are impacted by global economic conditions and may fluctuate in the future due to a number of factors that could reduce our net sales and profitability.
items.group: Risks Related to Our Business, Operations, and Industry

items.heading: We may lose sales if critical materials from concentrated sources become restricted or subject to export controls.
We are dependent on wafer foundries and other contractors, as are our SuperFlash and other licensees.
Our operating results may be adversely impacted by the financial viability and performance of our licensees, customers, distributors, resellers or suppliers.
We are highly dependent on foreign sales, suppliers, and operations, which exposes us to foreign political and economic risks.
Geopolitical instability in the Middle East may disrupt critical semiconductor materials, increase fuel costs, and adversely affect our ability to meet customer demand.
